title: Runtime API Preservation & Deprecation Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, enforceable semantic versioning and deprecation policy for the Redwood serving runtime that protects downstream customers while enabling timely evolution of the runtime. The playbook should cover: what constitutes a breaking change, required developer artifacts for approval, LTS channel commitments, staged rollout and rollback gates, and the upgrade tooling and CI checks that enforce compatibility. This ticket authors the policy, builds the checklist and CI guardrails, and wires the migration helper into the release pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A clear semver rule set documented (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH definitions for runtime and public REST/SDK surfaces)
Deprecation lifecycle rules documented (notification windows, warning surfaces, and removal timing)
LTS channel definitions and calendar (duration, security backports, supported minor releases) added to release docs
CI checks added to block merges that declare a breaking change without an approved migration plan
A developer-facing migration checklist and rupgrade CLI spec published
Rollout gates codified and integrated into GitHub Actions / release pipeline with observable thresholds
tasks: Draft semver policy text and examples (breaking change vs internal refactor) - @Marco
Create deprecation header and runtime warning semantics (X-Deprecation / telemetry) - @Sofia Nguyen
Design CI rejection rule and changelog linting for breaking-change label - @DevOps team
Implement canary rollout automation that ties to metrics and aborts on SLO regression - @Oncall/Platform
Prototype rupgrade CLI to transform config schemas and run compatibility tests - @InfraSDK
Write migration how-tos and templates for extension authors and internal SDKs - @DX team
decisions: Major version bump required if any public RPC/HTTP contract changes in the public runtime API that require consumer code changes
Minor versions allowed for additive behavior and new endpoints/features that are backwards-compatible
Patch releases reserved for bug fixes, security patches, and non-API behavioral fixes
Deprecation window: minimum of two major/minor releases (typically >= 6 months) before removal; LTS channels may extend retention for critical APIs
All breaking-change PRs must include a migration plan and a client-compatibility test matrix to be mergeable
Runtime will emit structured deprecation warnings in responses and log telemetry events to aid customer migrations
rollout_plan: 1) Pre-merge: PR must indicate semantic version impact via CHANGELOG/labels. 2) Nightly CI runs compatibility test matrix across 3 SDK versions. 3) Post-merge: Deploy to canary pool (1-2% traffic) for 24h. 4) Monitor error rate, latency P95, and customer-facing metrics for 48h. 5) If metrics stable, expand to 10% then 50% with 24h observation windows. 6) Full rollout only after automated gates satisfied or manual approval from Release Eng. Abort/rollback automatically if error budget exceeded or critical dashboards regress.
migration_tools: rupgrade CLI: schema migration, dry-run mode, config diff output
compatibility-test harness: runs cross-version integration tests between runtime and SDKs
changelog-linter: enforces semantic impact field in PRs
deprecation-notifier: generates deprecation emails and release notes snippets for docs
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stricter semver guarantees increase churn for engineers (more migration work) but reduce customer breakages. We prioritize customer stability: default to conservative classification and require cross-team sign-off for escalations. Plan to run a 90-day pilot with two internal teams before finalizing calendar for public LTS adoption.
